label: Telecommunications carrier / ISP
description: A regional communications service provider: an incumbent or competitive local exchange carrier or telephone cooperative, a regional mobile network operator, a cable operator (HFC / DOCSIS), a fiber or fixed-wireless ISP, an interconnected VoIP provider, or a covered 911 service provider (selective routers, ALI, ESInet / NGCS). Central offices, cell sites, headends, fiber rings and the NOC; OSS / NMS, the IP/MPLS core, mobile and voice cores, DNS and CPE management; billing and care systems holding CPNI; and the FCC outage, 911-notification and CPNI-breach clocks that go with them.

vocabulary.facility: the network (central offices, cell sites, headends and hubs, fiber routes, the core and the NOC)
vocabulary.public: subscribers and customers, and the PSAPs and public-safety users that depend on the network
vocabulary.frontline: NOC technicians, outside-plant splicers, cell-site technicians, care agents, retail store staff, network engineers

it: retail point-of-sale and care-agent desktop (SIM change, eSIM provisioning, port-out authorization)
customer portal, mobile app and the outage map / status page
email, identity (AD / SSO / MFA), VPN and privileged access management
SIEM / SOC, EDR, NetFlow collectors and DDoS detection and scrubbing
lawful-intercept / CALEA mediation and legal-demand case management
data warehouse with CPNI (call detail records, location history)
IVR / contact-center platform and outbound SMS / email notification
ot: OSS / NMS / EMS: fault management, performance, inventory and provisioning
NOC video wall and alarm correlation
IP/MPLS core and edge routers, route reflectors, BGP peering and RPKI validators
optical transport: DWDM, ROADMs, SONET rings, metro Ethernet
mobile core (EPC and 5G core), SMSC, SS7 / Diameter signaling and the signaling firewall
RAN: eNodeB / gNodeB at cell sites, microwave backhaul
voice: IMS core, softswitch, SBCs and TDM tandems
cable access: CMTS / vCMTS, headends, hubs and fiber nodes, DOCSIS provisioning
DNS resolvers, DHCP and AAA / RADIUS
911: selective routers / E911 tandems, ALI database, ESInet and NGCS
central-office power plants (rectifiers, batteries, generators), HVAC, PACS and CCTV

roles.name: Chief Operating Officer (Incident Commander / Crisis Management Team lead)
roles.description: Declares a major incident, approves service-affecting actions (isolating the core, taking a route down), the public statement and emergency spend.

roles.name: Chief Information Security Officer
roles.description: Owns the cyber investigation, the SOC, containment of compromised routers or OSS, FBI/CISA engagement and the threat-hunt scope.

roles.name: Director, Network Operations Center
roles.description: Owns the alarm picture, outage classification, restoration priority (TSP circuits first), change freezes and the NORS discovery time.

roles.name: Director, Core / IP Network Engineering
roles.description: Owns routing (BGP, MPLS), the mobile and voice cores; decides to filter, de-peer, roll back configurations or re-route.

roles.name: Director, Field Operations / Outside Plant
roles.description: Owns splicing crews, cell-site technicians, generator deployment and fueling, portable cell sites, 811 locates and right-of-way access.

roles.name: 911 / Public Safety Services Manager
roles.description: Owns PSAP relationships, the 30-minute 911 outage notification, ALI and selective-router health and ESInet / NGCS status.

roles.name: Regulatory Compliance Director (FCC / PUC liaison)
roles.description: Files NORS notification, initial and final reports, DIRS daily reports and state PUC outage reports; decides reportability with counsel (CPNI breach clock, SEC 8-K).

roles.name: Director, Corporate Communications (PIO)
roles.description: Owns press, social media, outage-map messaging and statements to elected officials.
